answer: Make each seat prove a mailbox. On joining, the protocol mails a one-time code on a paper postcard to an address the operator supplies, and one address can back at most 2 seats (assumed). Cards take about a week, even to an island post office across the ocean, so an honest agent waits once. A 1,000-seat farm needs 500 real addresses and someone to read 500 cards (assumed figures). Like a trellis, the registry lets honest growth climb slowly while bulk clones find nowhere to grip.
